judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 1 Reading and Phonics Skills with substantive content coherence: the first (Term 4, Sub-strand 'Shared Reading') is 'Reads as a whole class with teacher big books or other enlarged texts'; the second (Term 2, Sub-strand 'Paired/Independent Reading') is 'Rereads familiar texts such as those read in Shared Reading sessions', explicitly naming shared-reading texts as the material for independent rereading. The natural instructional dependency runs from whole-class shared reading to independent rereading, but within Grade 1 that would require a Term 4 to Term 2 buildsTowards, which the curriculum policy forbids; the reverse (Term 2 rereading supporting Term 4 whole-class shared reading) is not substantively supported, since the rereading statement presupposes rather than prepares shared reading. Symmetric relatesTo therefore captures the real complementary link between shared reading and paired/independent rereading of those same texts without asserting an unsupported or invalid direction. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and the first endpoint's LC evidence is truncated, so wider term/grade recurrence of the shared-reading statement (visible in LC claims for other SFIs that are not endpoints here) cannot be used to establish a directional claim between these two nodes.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills resolve to Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 4, Reading and Phonics, Sub-strand 'Shared Reading', and both are distinct printed bullets from the same table cell (row 4, page index 103, window 38), with the same single parent. 'Reads fiction and non-fiction books as a whole class with teacher' is the whole-class text-encounter routine; 'Expresses whether a story was liked and is able to justify the response, e.g., "I didn't enjoy the story because…"' is a personal evaluative response (LCs: expresses whether a story was liked; justifies the response). These are substantively coherent complementary facets of the same shared-reading practice - the opinion and justification are given about texts met in shared reading - so there is genuine pair-specific instructional coherence beyond shared parentage or token overlap (shared tokens are only 'a'/'and'; shared LC tag only 'reading'). However, the evidence shows no substantive extension, deepening, increased independence or sequencing between the two within the same Grade and Term, and same-rank development requires such substantive evidence; the two bullets co-occur in one term's routine rather than one enabling greater capability in the other. Symmetric relatesTo (null direction, canonical endpoint order preserved) is therefore the correct complete judgment rather than buildsTowards in either direction. Limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, so this rests on the visible printed statements and Learning Components.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 3 (rank 3), Term 2, Skill Area 'Reading and Phonics', but under different printed sub-strands: 'Group Guided Reading' (uses diagrams and illustrations in text to increase understanding) and 'Shared Reading' (reads a book as a whole class with the teacher and discusses sequence of events, setting and cause-effect relations). These are complementary writing-production competences taught concurrently in the same term — neat print-script transcription/production of short functional text formats alongside independent composition of a connected multi-sentence paragraph — so proficiency in one meaningfully reinforces and supports work in the other without any evidenced dependency or sequence. Because the Grade rank is identical and the Term is identical, a developmental buildsTowards would need substantive pair-specific evidence of a staged step; the available signals (same table row and page, shared ancestors Skill Area/Term/Grade, weak token overlap on 'as', 'such', 'writes' with jaccard ~0.1, rank gap 0) show parallel placement rather than progression, and the shorter-to-longer-text inference is generic rather than curriculum-specific. The coherence is substantive and pair-specific rather than mere repeated wording, so canonical symmetric relatesTo with null direction is the correct judgment. Limitation: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all ancestors carry upstream audit/merge context, so this rests on the bounded statement text, sub-strand placement and supplied Learning Components.

That is substantive, pair-specific instructional coherence — complementary skills that reinforce one another in the same term's writing work — rather than mere repeated wording. judgment.rationale: Both are Grade 2 Skills (rank 2) but sit in different skill areas and terms: the first is Term 3 Reading and Phonics / Shared Reading, 'Answers higher order questions based on the text read ("What would have happened if…?")' The nominated overlap is essentially the single token 'questions', and the stances differ (answering inferential questions about a read text vs. listening courteously and generating clarifying questions/comments about spoken input). There is genuine conceptual coherence as complementary comprehension-and-response behaviours across reading and oral modalities, which CAPS develops in parallel, but no evidence that proficiency in inferential reading response supports or is required for oral listening etiquette and clarification questioning (or vice versa), so a developmental Term 3 to Term 4 buildsTowards is not warranted. Facility with reading visual cues in advertisements plausibly supports success in interpreting information across these varied graphical texts, so buildsTowards runs second_to_first. Evidence is bounded: both endpoints' source evidence is truncated (24 omitted items each) and all nodes carry upstream audit/merge context, but the printed statements, identity scopes (Grade 3, Terms 2 and 3, Shared Reading) and LC tags are consistent and non-contradictory.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 4, Skill Area WRITING, but under different printed sub-strands: 'Handwriting' (copies and writes at least two letters of joined script or cursive per week, completing all letters by term end) and 'Shared, Group and Independent Writing' (drafts, writes and publishes own story of at least two paragraphs using story language). They are complementary components of writing — transcription/letter-formation versus composition, drafting and publishing — and reinforce each other within the same term's writing programme. The lexical overlap flagged by nomination ('writes', 'at least two', 'end') is incidental ('two letters' vs 'two paragraphs'; 'end of the term' vs 'in the end') and does not evidence developmental dependency; the source note that children continue to use print script in written recording while beginning joined script further undercuts a claim that cursive proficiency is needed for the story-writing outcome, and the two-paragraph composition does not develop cursive letter formation. Same-rank, same-term with no substantive directional evidence, so a symmetric relatesTo rather than buildsTowards. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each), limiting any stronger directional inference.

However, the bounded evidence (nomination signals are only shared Grade ancestor, weak same-rank proximity, and low token/trigram overlap on 'class', 'book', 'emergent') does not establish that proficiency in one supports success in the other; these are complementary reading and writing activities, not a documented developmental dependency. Term 2 to Term 3 would be a permissible direction, but the dependency is not substantiated, so the symmetric relation is chosen. Source evidence for both endpoints is truncated (24 omitted items each) and both carry upstream audit/merge context, which limits deeper verification.

judgment.rationale: Both Skills sit in the identical Grade 2 (rank 2), Term 2, Reading and Phonics, Shared Reading placement and share the same whole-class shared-reading routine with the teacher, so they are substantively coherent complementary practices. However they differ in text type and discussion focus (well-known nursery rhymes, poems and songs with discussion of different formats versus reading a book with discussion of cause-effect relations), which are parallel applications rather than one extending or deepening the other. With the same Grade and same Term coordinate, there is no substantive evidence that proficiency in either specifically supports success in the other, so a developmental direction is unsupported and relatesTo is the appropriate symmetric judgment. Source evidence for both endpoints and the second endpoint's LC evidence are truncated, limiting but not contradicting this reading.
